Transmission gate-based 12T SRAM cell for biomedical application
The Objective of 8T SRAM (Static Random-Access Memory) cell architecture is to provide a
balance between read and write stability, this work explores the design and implementation
of nextgeneration biological memory systems. The investigation of these improvements is
driven by the growing need for effective memory systems in biomedical applications, which
necessitates meeting stringent standards while boosting performance, stability, and
dependability. This work intends to open the door for revolutionary developments in medical
technology by evaluating the viability of integrating these modified SRAM cells into memory
arrays for biomedical devices. The study includes a review of the literature, a methodology,
and a thorough assessment of the suggested changes, including stability, reliability, and
energy efficiency studies. To demonstrate the viability of the improved memory systems in
biomedical applications, real-world case studies are carried out. The results have the potential
to significantly advance healthcare technologies.
